content:
Circle \(C\): \((x+1)^2+(y-4)^2=4\), so center \(O=(-1,4)\), radius \(2\).

For \(y^2=8x\), focus \(F=(2,0)\), directrix \(x=-2\). Thus for \(P\) on the parabola,
\[
d=|PF|.
\]
For any \(Q\in C\),
\[
|PQ|\ge |PO|-|OQ|=|PO|-2.
\]
So
\[
d+|PQ|\ge |PF|+|PO|-2\ge |FO|-2.
\]
Now
\[
|FO|=\sqrt{(2+1)^2+(0-4)^2}=5,
\]
hence
\[
d+|PQ|\ge 5-2=3.
\]

Equality occurs when \(P\) lies on segment \(FO\). The line \(FO\) is
\[
y=\frac{8-4x}{3}.
\]
Intersect with \(y^2=8x\):
\[
\left(\frac{8-4x}{3}\right)^2=8x
\]
\[
2x^2-17x+8=0
\]
\[
x=\frac12 \quad \text{or} \quad x=8.
\]
The point on segment \(FO\) is \(x=\frac12\), giving \(P=\left(\frac12,2\right)\). Thus equality is achievable.

\[
\boxed{3}
\]
